title: HumanSampleResult
description: raw/_provenance/<run_id>/human_sample_result.json — the ANSWER half of the human spot-check (A4/B11). A HUMAN writes this file: for every cell human_sample_plan.json named, what they saw when they opened the original. It is the only thing that makes `reread_channel: human` true anywhere in the archive — 「人工核对过」 asserted without a matching verdict here is a claim with no record, and the validator treats it as one. Two verdicts of `mismatch` make the archive NOT DELIVERABLE: one mismatch is a field to re-read, two say the transcription pass is unreliable on THIS material and the unsampled pages carry the same unmeasured error rate.

run_id.description: Must match the run_id of the human_sample_plan.json sitting beside it.

performed_by.description: Who did the check — a person or a named role, not a model id. An unattributed human check is not a record of one. This is an accountability field, and it is not patient content: it must never carry a PATIENT's name.

performed_at.description: When the check was performed. Undated means unauditable: it cannot be placed before or after the re-transcription it is supposed to validate.

verdicts.description: One entry per planned sample item. A PARTIAL result is worse than none — it reads downstream as a completed spot-check while covering only the cells that happened to agree — so the validator requires every planned item to appear here.

label.description: Verbatim, and identical to the plan's label for the same cell — the join key.

verdict.description: THREE values, and the third one is the point. `match` = the original says what the archive says. `mismatch` = it does not. `unreadable` = the person could not tell, because the cell is illegible, cropped, or obscured on the original — which is NOT a match and must never be recorded as one. Collapsing unreadable into match is how an unverifiable cell becomes a verified one; collapsing it into mismatch would instead condemn a correct transcription for the page's own quality. Any fourth spelling (「ok」, 「pass」, 「n/a」) is a schema violation, because a verdict nothing recognises is a verdict nothing counts.

observed_value.description: Optional: what the checker actually read off the original. Required in practice for a mismatch, since the correction is what the re-read needs.
